As urban heat intensifies, so does the demand for cooling - and with it, the urgency for inclusive, digital-first energy solutions.
 
Electricity generation from fossil fuels rose 1.4% from 2023 to 2024, driven largely by increased cooling demand in cities. Since the 1980s, the number of extreme heat days in urban centers has tripled - fueled by the twin problems of urban heat island effect & climate change.
 
By 2050, global installed cooling capacity is projected to nearly triple; from 22 TW in 2022 to 58 TW. But it’s not just about cooling homes and buildings. Data centers, the backbone of the AI revolution, consume over 40%+ of their energy for cooling alone, even more in warmer regions, to operate optimally.
 
This  isn’t just an energy and climate issue; it’s an opportunity to reshape how we govern and deliver smarter, more equitable, energy transitions:
 
🔹 AI for smarter governance:
Transparent, data-driven, tools make energy systems more transparent and accountable. They help optimize resources and support evidence-based infrastructure planning.
 
🔹 Equity through digital tools:
Kenya’s integration of digital tools like the Energy Access Explorer helped boost electricity access rates from 20% to 75% in under a decade; illustrating that data-led approaches can drive inclusive energy access.
 
🔹 A just digital transition:
Without inclusive policy frameworks, digital innovation risks deepening social inequalities. Equitable robust digital infrastructures and fair data governance are essential for climate justice
 
As global temperatures continue to break records, our policies, technologies, and infrastructure must keep pace of digital change. We need to ensure that cooling, connectivity and clean energy can reach everyone everywhere.
